posts.author: Joe Farina
posts.content_md:
I noticed the following 40mW blue laser:

[http://www.edmundoptics.com/onlinecatal ... uctID=2798](http://www.edmundoptics.com/onlinecatalog/displayproduct.cfm?productID=2798) 

I haven't been following diode laser technology for years, but there must be a 445nm diode out there (?) This wavelength would be excellent for color holography, unlike 405nm. The 40mW power level might be just sufficient, if the diode could be stabilized, which is a big question mark.

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md:
At least that package has a TEC already. What exactly does the spec:

TEM 00, M2 < 1.5 

mean? Does that mean there is a faint second temporal mode?

posts.author: dcgman
posts.content_md:
M2 is "M squared", and is a measure of the beam quality.

Read about it here:

[http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beam_parameter_product](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beam_parameter_product)

posts.author: Joe Farina
posts.content_md:
I see that Power Technolgy has those 50mW 445nm diodes in stock, as well as some 20mW 473nm ones.

[http://www.powertechnology.com/diodes.asp](http://www.powertechnology.com/diodes.asp) 

No prices were given: I'm sure they're horrendous. Imagine the fear of blowing one.

posts.author: Joe Farina
posts.content_md:
Someone on alt.lasers indicated that the 50mW 445nm diode goes for $3000. They are new, like the 473nm ones, apparently.

The 405nm diodes are much more accessible nowadays, being pulled from equipment. This may be an interesting approach to acquiring blue diodes in general. After all, the 315's many of us now have are the result of the same thing, being removed from graphic arts equipment, and made available to Sal.
